desc:
People stand in a line from left to right; heights[i] is the height of person i, and all heights are distinct. Person i can see person j (j > i) if everybody standing strictly between them is shorter than both heights[i] and heights[j]. (Neighbors always see each other.)

Return an array answer where answer[i] is the number of people to the right of person i that person i can see.

Example: heights = [10, 6, 8, 5, 11, 9] gives [3, 1, 2, 1, 1, 0]. Person 0 (height 10) sees the people of height 6, 8 and 11; the person of height 5 is hidden behind the 8, and the 9 behind the 11.
hints: Person i keeps seeing to the right until the first person at least as tall as i blocks the view for everyone behind. Describe exactly which people are seen up to and including that blocker.

Looking along the line, the people i sees (before a blocker) are the successive 'record highs' of the people to its right, i.e. a monotonic structure. Process people from right to left and keep exactly that structure.

Sweep from right to left with a stack of heights that is decreasing from bottom to top (the top is the nearest person). For person i: pop every shorter person and count each as seen; if the stack is still non-empty, the new top is taller and is also seen (count one more). Push i.
editorial: Sweep from right to left and maintain a stack that contains the people who are potentially visible to someone further left: from the top (nearest) to the bottom (farthest) their heights increase, because a person hidden behind a taller person nearer to the viewer can never be seen by anybody to the left of that taller person.

For person i, every stack element that is shorter than i is visible, since everything between them and i is shorter than that element (it was a record high), so pop each and add one. The first element that is taller than i is also visible (everyone between is shorter than i), but it blocks everything behind it, so add one more and stop. Elements popped are hidden from everyone left of i, because i is taller and nearer. Then push i.
Each person is pushed once and popped at most once: O(n) time, O(n) space. Distinct heights keep the rule 'shorter vs taller' unambiguous.
solution:
def visibleToTheRight(heights):
    n = len(heights)
    answer = [0] * n
    stack = []  # heights, increasing from top (nearest) to bottom (farthest)
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        seen = 0
        while stack and stack[-1] < heights[i]:
            stack.pop()
            seen += 1
        if stack:
            seen += 1
        answer[i] = seen
        stack.append(heights[i])
    return answer
